Liam — thanks for the quick responses. See answers below and notes on where we’ll add evidence vs. narrative in the SIG sheet: 

1) Customer-managed KMS/HSM:
- Hosted: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS using a BYOK flow for customers in AWS accounts (we can rotate keys on your schedule).
- Private/on-prem: yes, we support integrations with on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11 and can configure the runtime to use your HSM for key operations.
(Evidence: configuration guide + sample key policy will be attached in the next email.)

2) Default data retention:
- Request payloads: retained for 30 days by default on Hosted API; customers can configure shorter retention or disable retention for Private deployments.
- Logs/metrics: retained 90 days in the console; extended retention available as an add-on.
(Evidence: retention policy excerpt available as PDF — I’ve attached a high-level excerpt in the SOC2 overview.)

3) Subprocessors:
- We publish an internal subprocessors list and maintain it in our compliance Drive. We proactively notify customers on material changes quarterly and on-demand for contract-critical updates.
(Evidence: current subprocessors export will be attached; for the SIG we can paste the list into the subcontractors tab.)

Action items from our side:
- Marissa will populate the encryption and auth sections with technical detail and config examples.
- I’ll populate the data residency, retention, and subprocessors sections and attach the supporting excerpts.
- We’ll return a filled-first-pass SIG by end of day Tue 2026-04-27 as proposed. If you need it sooner, let us know.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute call Wed 2026-04-28 to walk through any high-risk answers — does 10:00 PT work for you and Sarah?
